title: Dynegy Moss Landing Power Plant Hybrid: EPA Agreement for Moss Landing Battery Removal
summary: EPA announced an enforceable agreement requiring Vistra to conduct and fund supervised removal of fire-affected batteries. Entity test: The later official record verifies corrective-action progress and an incident boundary while blocking a facility-wide availability or return-to-service claim.
key_findings: The agreement requires work plans, monitoring, emergency response, community involvement, and EPA oversight during removal.
Alternative-explanation test: Tests regulator-verified corrective-action obligations and incident-response conditions.
Compatibility: The records concern the 300 MW fire-affected battery building inside the broader Moss Landing complex; they are not a common 750 MW plant-performance observation.
why_it_matters: This record either supplies a later compatible observation or tests a named Phase 56C alternative explanation without turning association into causal proof.
ftfn_relevance: Preserves the Phase 56C parent dossier and stable entity identifier.
Maps the record to named alternative explanations.
Separates observed result, attribution, independent validation, and unresolved denominators.
evidence_limits: An enforceable removal obligation and later progress do not establish root cause, facility return to service, availability, dispatch, revenue, or reliability effects.
Regulator-verified work status; root cause, complete removal, return to service, and plant-wide performance remain unresolved.
No causal effect, ranking, composite score, readiness score, or unsupported cross-entity comparison is supported.
